The infobox also lists the Military Government of the Philippine Islands and the Sultanate of Sulu as predecessors.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row of its own: the United States row draws the Philippines in this period). Infobox area '1903: 297,916 km2' and '1918: 296,296 km2', which is the whole archipelago (the grid's Philippines is about 266,300 km2, ratio 0.89, the difference being islets the res-5 grid drops). The shape is the whole country for the whole life, because the page gives no territorial change between 1899 and 1946 other than sub-provincial reorganisations (Batanes 1907 and 1909); the Moro Province (Mindanao and Sulu) is listed on the page without a date. In 1899-1901 the Americans held only part of this land (the First Philippine Republic held most of the rest); the contest events below record that, and the first-philippine-republic dossier draws the republic's land.

ledger.note: 11 April 1899: the Insular Government is established. The page: it 'was established on April 11, 1899, upon ratification of the 1898 Treaty of Paris' (infobox 'Established: April 11, 1899'; 'Treaty of Paris ratified: April 11, 1899'). It was 'preceded by the Military Government of the Philippine Islands'. The land is the archipelago the treaty ceded (the infobox area 297,916 km2 in 1903).

union.text: Manila, held by the Americans after 13 August 1898

region.text: the land the First Philippine Republic held in 1898-99 (infobox: 'most of which it occupied except Manila and parts of Mindanao'): the archipelago without Manila and, as the page does not say which parts, without Mindanao

ledger.note: April 1899: the American claim is contested by the First Philippine Republic. The First Philippine Republic page: 'On February 4, fighting erupted in Manila between American and Filipino forces'; the republic held 'most of' the archipelago 'except Manila and parts of Mindanao' (infobox). The war began before this dossier's start (the Insular Government dates from the treaty's ratification), so the contest opens with the dossier; the page does not map the republic's land by province.

region.text: the northern Luzon provinces of the republic's last capitals: Nueva Vizcaya (Bayombong), Kalinga (Lubuagan) and Isabela (Palanan)

ledger.note: 19 April 1901: the republic is dissolved de jure. The First Philippine Republic page: 'Palanan, Isabela - On March 23, 1901, General Aguinaldo was captured by American forces'; 'Following his capture, Aguinaldo announced allegiance to the United States on April 19, 1901' (infobox 'De jure dissolution: 19 April 1901', 'De facto dissolution: 16 April 1902'). The land still held out is the three northern provinces of the republic's last capitals (the researcher's reading).

4 July 1901: civil government begins. The page: 'On July 4, 1901, executive authority over the islands was transferred to the president of the Philippine Commission' (the civil governor, in place of the military governor); 'On July 4, 1902, the civil governor became the sole executive authority of the islands'. The page's Organic Act date is 1 July 1902 (infobox) or only '1902' (text).

15 November 1935: the Commonwealth replaces the Insular Government. The Commonwealth page: 'The Commonwealth government was inaugurated on the morning of November 15, 1935'; the Insular Government page: 'In 1935, the Insular Government was replaced by the Commonwealth' and 'It was reorganized in 1935 in preparation for later independence'.

24 December 1941: the capital leaves Manila. The Commonwealth page: 'Corregidor served as a temporary capital from December 24, 1941' (Manila being held by the enemy 'between December 24, 1941, and February 27, 1945'); the Japanese had launched 'a surprise attack on the Philippines on the morning of December 8, 1941'.
2 January 1942: Manila falls to Japan. The Commonwealth page: Manila 'occupied by the Japanese on January 2, 1942'.

May 1942: the rest of the archipelago is Japanese-held. The Commonwealth page: fighting on Bataan and Corregidor continued 'until the final surrender of joint United States-Philippine forces in May 1942' (no day given); the page says that 'Japan occupied the Philippines' for 1942-45. The land outside Manila is read as the whole archipelago, though the page does not date the fall of the Visayas and Mindanao.

27 February 1945: Manila is back under the Commonwealth. The Commonwealth page: infobox 'Restoration: February 27, 1945'; Manila was held by enemy forces 'between December 24, 1941, and February 27, 1945'; the Allies 'landed on Leyte on October 20, 1944'.

27 February 1945: the Commonwealth is restored at Manila (infobox 'Restoration: February 27, 1945'). The government had been in exile at Washington from 12 March 1942 (infobox 'Government-in-exile: March 12, 1942').

2 September 1945: Japan's surrender ends the occupation. The Commonwealth page: 'Japan's official surrender in August 1945, which was signed on September 2 in Tokyo Bay'. The page does not date the end of fighting in the countryside, so the date is the surrender's, applied to the land outside Manila.

ledger.note: 4 July 1946: the Philippines become independent. The Commonwealth page: 'The Commonwealth officially ended on July 4, 1946' (the US 'recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946, as scheduled'); infobox 'Independence: July 4, 1946'.

wars.name: Philippine-American War

union.text: Manila, held by the Americans after 13 August 1898

zones.text: the land the First Philippine Republic held in 1898-99 (infobox: 'most of which it occupied except Manila and parts of Mindanao'): the archipelago without Manila and, as the page does not say which parts, without Mindanao

wars.outcome: American victory: Malolos captured on 31 March 1899, Aguinaldo captured on 23 March 1901 and the republic dissolved de jure on 19 April 1901 (de facto 16 April 1902).
wars.note: The First Philippine Republic page dates the fighting from 4 February 1899; the war's end year (1902) is that page's de facto dissolution. The first-philippine-republic and united-states-of-america dossiers carry the same war.

wars.name: Japanese invasion and occupation of the Philippines

zones.text: the Philippine archipelago, as ceded by the Treaty of Paris

wars.outcome: Japanese victory in May 1942 (final surrender of joint US-Philippine forces), then Allied reconquest: landing on Leyte on 20 October 1944, Manila retaken by 27 February 1945, surrender signed 2 September 1945.
wars.note: The page names no battle dates beyond 8 December 1941, 24 December 1941, 2 January 1942, May 1942, 20 October 1944 and 27 February 1945.

certainty.note: The Americans held only part of the archipelago while the First Philippine Republic held most of it; the American claim covers the whole.
An archipelago ceded by treaty: its limits are the coasts; the Moro Province (Mindanao and Sulu) was governed within it.
A government in exile (from 12 March 1942) with the islands under Japanese occupation; the occupation events carry the land.
The coasts of the archipelago until independence on 4 July 1946.

sources.title: Insular Government of the Philippine Islands
sources.note: Established 11 April 1899 on ratification of the Treaty of Paris; 4 July 1901 and 4 July 1902 transfers of executive authority; Organic Act 1 July 1902 (infobox); area 297,916 km2 (1903) and 296,296 km2 (1918); capital Manila; replaced by the Commonwealth in 1935; Batanes 1907 and 1909.

sources.title: Commonwealth of the Philippines
sources.note: Inaugurated 15 November 1935; Japanese attack 8 December 1941; Corregidor temporary capital from 24 December 1941; Manila occupied 2 January 1942; final surrender May 1942; government-in-exile 12 March 1942; Leyte 20 October 1944; restoration 27 February 1945; surrender signed 2 September 1945; ended 4 July 1946.

sources.title: First Philippine Republic
sources.note: Fighting from 4 February 1899; Malolos captured 31 March 1899; Aguinaldo captured 23 March 1901 and allegiance on 19 April 1901 (infobox de jure dissolution), de facto 16 April 1902; territory 'most of which it occupied except Manila and parts of Mindanao'.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch. Three pages opened (Insular Government, Commonwealth, First Philippine Republic). The Cliopatria United States row and the united-states-of-america dossier both draw the Philippines from 1898-99 to 1946; this dossier is the colony as a state of its own, and eu/am reconciliation should either drop the Philippines from the US shape for these years or let this dossier carry it (the dossier's keyframe is the whole country). Unsettled: (1) the start: 11 April 1899 (ratification, per the page) against 4 February 1899, when the war began (the US dossier opens the contest then); this dossier opens its contest with the dossier; (2) the Tydings-McDuffie Act is dated 24 March 1934 (footnote) and 15 November 1935 (infobox) on the Commonwealth page, and 'of 1934' in the Insular page's text; the rename follows the inauguration, 15 November 1935; (3) the Organic Act is 1 July 1902 (Insular infobox) or '1902' (text), and was not made a ledger event; (4) the Moro Province, the Bates Treaty, the Treaty of Washington of 7 November 1900 (Cagayan de Sulu and Sibutu) and the Turtle and Mangsee Islands are not on the opened pages, so no event is dated; (5) the Japanese occupation is two events (Manila on 2 January 1942; the rest, May 1942, a month with no day), the Visayas and Mindanao falling at dates the page does not give; the united-states-of-america dossier dates the occupation to May 1942 as one event; (6) the Japanese-sponsored Second Philippine Republic (the page names only 'the Second Philippine Republic' headed by José P. Laurel and lists the Philippine Executive Commission as a 1942 successor entity) needs a dossier of its own, outside this batch's scope (se-04, jk-01); (7) the government in exile at Washington (12 March 1942) is not drawn as a capital; (8) the 1899-1901 contest regions follow the first-philippine-republic dossier's shapes (the researcher's reading of the infobox); (9) type colony, colour family americas. Gazetteer: Manila, Mindanao, Corregidor, Nueva Vizcaya, Kalinga, Isabela.
